body:
Good morning, Kern County. It's Friday, September 11 — the 25th anniversary of the 2001 attacks, and a morning that starts mild at 77 degrees under a moderate-air-quality sky before climbing toward 99. The day's headline belongs to Arvin: after more than a year without a police chief, the small community to the south welcomes its new leader Monday, and residents are already calling the hire a bridge-builder.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's heaviest response came just after 2 a.m., when officers were sent to a Mohawk Street block after a caller reported someone inside a vacant unit. The caller described a loud argument, a woman screaming for help and a man yelling, and two people were seen on a rear landing before fleeing toward a road to the north. A search of the area followed, with descriptions of both broadcast to responding units. Minutes later, at 2:27 a.m., crews investigating a separate call requested a reinforced structure fire response and handled it as a structure fire.

Earlier in the evening, around 9:20 p.m., a caller at a Bakersfield lodging property reported smoke coming from inside a room. Fire crews arrived to find a small fire in a restroom and took care of it. Over at Hart Park, a passerby flagged down a park ranger about a motorcycle crash just beyond the east entrance; an engine was sent, but no patient was found at the scene, and the sheriff's office stayed on to handle the call. An officer working the Olive Drive overpass also called for a tow after a bicyclist was involved in a collision there, with eastbound traffic moving at the time.

The rest of the log leaned on disturbances and welfare checks, with a string of domestic-related calls spread across the county. Officers responded to reports of threats on Linden Avenue near Magnolia, a disturbance involving a woman and her ex-husband on a Meeks Avenue block, and a woman whose ex-boyfriend fled north toward the airport in an older black SUV after an incident on the Beardsley Avenue block. Deputies searched for a shirtless man in his 30s after an assault with a pole on North Lincoln Street north of Pierce Road, and looked into a threat on a Water Street apartment block. A welfare check in Bakersfield turned more serious when a family member reportedly made threatening statements and told dispatchers he had firearms and explosives. Crews also handled an abandoned barbecue pit at a Mojave apartment complex on Barstow Road and a water heater leaking into a home on the Teal Street block.

## Today's weather

Expect a warm one: the high should reach near 99, with a low around 70 overnight. At this hour the thermometer at Meadows Field reads 77, a comfortable start before the heat builds through the afternoon.

There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no fires are being tracked in the morning report. Air quality sits at 65 — moderate — so sensitive groups may want to take it easy outdoors in the heat of the day. The evening should cool off nicely for anyone heading to outdoor plans.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that Arvin is preparing to welcome its newest police chief Monday, ending more than a year without one.** Chief Cecilio Velasco's ability to speak Spanish is the detail residents keep coming back to. The city is home to a large Spanish-speaking population, and community members who spoke with 23ABC said the hire could close a longstanding gap between neighbors and law enforcement. One resident of eight years said she feels safer knowing officers will have someone who can address them directly; another, who has lived in Arvin for more than two decades, called it a relief to be able to express concerns in her own language. Velasco starts Monday.

**According to KGET 17, two people have been sentenced to life without the possibility of parole in connection with a 2024 shooting in Lamont.** The sentences mark a major outcome for a case that has weighed on the small community south of Bakersfield, and they close a difficult chapter for the families involved. No further details were available in the brief report.

**23ABC's coverage of the 9/11 anniversary found that for local students, the attacks are now history, not memory.** Bakersfield High School student David Lozano told the outlet he understands the casualties and severity of that day but carries little of the emotional weight of those who lived through it. Other students expressed a deep sense of empathy for the lives lost, and one said the day should always be kept in honor of those who died. A 2021 California law encourages schools to hold a moment of silence each September 11, though districts have flexibility in how the lessons are taught — and professors say the tragedy is increasingly presented as a historic event rather than lived experience.

**KGET 17 reports that a proposed Alzheimer's day program is seeking nonprofit status with hopes of relocating to the existing ADAKC building.** The move could give Kern County families a dedicated daytime option for loved ones living with memory loss, a need that has grown as the valley's population ages. The plan's next step depends on the nonprofit designation coming through.

**23ABC also announced that Bakersfield police Capt. Ted King will officially become the department's new assistant chief on Sept. 21.** King, a Bakersfield native and 22-year veteran of the force, grew up here, attended North High School and Bakersfield College, served in the U.S. Army with two deployments to the Middle East, and joined BPD in 2005. He worked patrol, robbery-homicide and special operations before becoming a captain in 2022. He told 23ABC he's grateful for the appointment, and that his focus will be supporting Chief Brent Stratton's vision and making sure the community feels safe. King fills the spot left open when Stratton became chief in May.

## Something good

A World War II veteran in Bakersfield has reached a remarkable milestone: a 105th birthday celebration, with the community gathering to honor a lifetime of service and longevity. It's a sweet reminder that Kern County knows how to take care of its own.

There was also a warm moment this week on National Police Woman Day, when KGET 17 tipped its cap to the first groundbreaking woman to serve on the Bakersfield Police Department. Her trailblazing path opened doors for every woman who has worn the badge since — a small, worthy salute.

## Coming up this week

The public calendar gets started today: the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee meets at noon, a chance for residents to weigh in on the city's cleanup and greening efforts. Monday brings the Fire Civil Service Commission at 3 p.m., and the Miscelaneous Civil Service Commission follows Tuesday at 2 p.m. — both open to the public.

Wednesday is the big day at City Hall, with the City Council holding two sessions: agenda item 330 at 3:30 p.m. and agenda 515 at 5:15 p.m. Thursday evening, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. Anyone wanting to follow along can check the city's meeting portal for agendas and remote viewing options. Also Monday, Arvin's new police chief starts — the story neighbors have been waiting more than a year to see.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full week: comedian Max Amini takes the stage Saturday night, country singer Clay Walker brings his "Doin' What I Love" tour on Sunday, and the Cults & Classics series screens "Fargo" on Monday night. Next Friday brings "It's A 2000s Party," and Sept. 21 wraps the run with "What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?" — plenty of ways to close out the heat of September in air-conditioned style.

And today, of course, marks 25 years since Sept. 11, 2001. Two remembrance ceremonies are planned in Bakersfield, and Bakersfield Now is asking neighbors whether they plan to attend one of them. However you mark the day — a quiet moment of reflection, a ceremony, or a conversation with someone who remembers — it's worth pausing for the lives lost and the day that changed everything.
